title: Warm-handoff email deviates from the spec's pinned copy in ways the spec itself does not document
evidence:
+- Body: `Hi {landlord_name},` + `Couldn't reach {referee_name} ({applicant_full_name}'s referee). You can take over from the application page.` (§7.9 verbatim) + `We've messaged them {attempt_count} times over the last 4 days. The attempt log:` + one line per attempt `• {at}: {channel}, {outcome} {detail}` + `Their contact details and the same log are on the application page.` + CTA `Open the application` → `{application_url}`.
+      "Their contact details and the same log are on the application page. If they complete the form anyway, it still shows up there.",
+    detail -> " (" <> email_client.escape_html(detail) <> ")"
+- Removed an extra co-nudge line ("If X has already replied, you can ignore this.") I had added beyond the deck: the A2 guard (co-nudge only fires when the form was never opened, no draft) already covers that case; verbatim-minus-documented-deviations is the contract.
detail: The story's own contract is verbatim-minus-documented-deviations, enforced by removing an added co-nudge line. Yet the warm-handoff adds an undocumented sentence and renders attempt lines as '(detail)' with parens where the spec pins '{outcome} {detail}' bare. Spec and tests now disagree on the copy contract.
recommended_fix: Either update the spec's pinned copy and deviations register to cover the added sentence and the parenthesised detail format, or revert the template to the pinned strings.

title: Reminder-1 and co-nudge greeting-split capitalisation deviates from pinned copy but only reminder-2's is documented
evidence:
+- Body: `Hi {referee_first_name}, a quick reminder about the reference form for {applicant_full_name}'s rental application. If you've already started, the same link picks up where you left off: {form_url}`
+- Body: `Hi {applicant_first_name}, we've invited {referee_name} to complete your reference, but haven't heard back yet.
+          "A quick reminder about the reference form for "
+      "We've invited "
+- Two test-then-copy reconciliation fixes caught by the suite: sentence-initial capitals in reminder-2 copy ("This is our last message"), and the possessive-suffix apostrophe staying RAW in email HTML
detail: The spec pins greetings flowing into lowercase continuations; the implementation splits 'Hi X,' into its own paragraph and capitalises the next sentence in reminder-1 and co-nudge too, but the debug log documents this reconciliation only for reminder-2.
recommended_fix: Add the reminder-1 and co-nudge greeting-split capitalisation to the spec's documented deviations so the copy contract stays accurate.

title: Unresolved '??' placeholder shipped in committed docs (spec and send.gleam doc comment)
evidence:
+  - [x] T4.2 `pub type RefereeMessage` — wraps the shared `messages.RefereeContext` + `to_email: Option(String)` + `to_phone: Option(String)` (the sweep resolves corrected ?? snapshot before calling).
+/// A referee-directed message: the rendering context plus the resolved
+/// effective contacts (the sweep applies corrected ?? snapshot before
+/// calling — AD-7's effective-contact rule lives with the caller).
detail: 'corrected ?? snapshot' is an undecided placeholder, not prose. It ships in both the story spec and the module doc that rc3-5's implementer will read to wire the sweep.
recommended_fix: Replace '??' with the intended wording (e.g. 'corrected-else-snapshot' or the actual rule name from AD-7) in both files.

title: first_name's [] branch is unreachable and contradicts its own doc comment
detail: string.split of an empty (trimmed) string yields [""], so the [first, ..] arm always matches and the [] arm is dead. Worse, if [] ever did match it would return the untrimmed raw name, contradicting the documented '' behaviour.
recommended_fix: Drop the unreachable [] arm by matching on the trimmed input first, or restructure so the empty case returns "" explicitly.

title: first_name is exported but has no production caller anywhere in the diff
detail: RefereeContext takes referee_first_name pre-derived and no template or send helper calls first_name; only the test does. The sweep (rc3-5) is the intended caller, so this is public API committed ahead of any consumer.
recommended_fix: Acceptable if rc3-5 lands next; otherwise note in the doc comment that the caller is the sweep, or defer the helper to rc3-5.

title: Warm-handoff with an empty attempt log tells the landlord 'We've tried to reach them 0 times over the last 4 days'
evidence:
+    <> email_paragraph(
+      "We've tried to reach them "
+      <> count
+      <> " times over the last 4 days. The attempt log:",
+    )
+pub fn warm_handoff_empty_log_renders_honestly_test() {
+  string.contains(html, "No attempts recorded.") |> should.be_true
+  string.contains(html, "0 times") |> should.be_true
detail: The test pins '0 times' plus 'No attempts recorded.' as the honest empty state, but a landlord-facing email saying 'tried to reach them 0 times over the last 4 days' is nonsense copy; the count sentence should be omitted when the log is empty.
recommended_fix: When attempts is [], skip the count paragraph and keep only 'No attempts recorded.'; update the test accordingly.

title: item_style hardcodes the brand font stack instead of composing the brand_font const
evidence:
+const brand_font = "'DM Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif"
+
+const item_style = "font-family: 'DM Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; color: #2D2D2D; line-height: 1.6; margin: 0 0 8px 0;"
detail: The same font stack is duplicated verbatim one line below the const that exists to hold it; a brand-font change would silently drift the attempt-log <li> styling from every other element.
recommended_fix: Make item_style a fn or const concatenation reusing brand_font, mirroring how email_paragraph/notice_footer compose it.
